title: The Focusing Question
coreMove: Use one leverage question to narrow from many possible moves to the next move that changes the rest.
sourcePressure: Part 2 introduces the Focusing Question as the operational tool for leverage: narrow toward the next consequential move without pretending certainty is guaranteed.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Quoting a slogan and treating it as a magic answer generator.

hook: A single choice changes the whole day
The real priority is hiding under the busy work
The Focusing Question as a generic focus opener
counterintuition: Focus is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: Set a timer and list priorities
Write down your one thing without a concrete context
examples: generic office worker choosing email or strategy

exampleSpecs.domain: busy dermatology practice reducing biopsy delays
exampleSpecs.stakes: abnormal results are waiting too long for callbacks
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks which one fix makes callbacks easier and chooses specimen-label routing before patient scripts or portal redesign
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a biopsy label tray beside a phone log with red circles

exampleSpecs.domain: boatyard repair schedule before launch season
exampleSpecs.stakes: owners threaten refunds if hull work slips
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he asks which repair unlocks the most launches and moves the shared lift to the cracked keel job first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a boat lift chain hanging over a hull with chalked crack lines

exampleSpecs.stakes: volunteers are free but learners keep dropping off
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks which one change makes attendance easier and chooses evening childcare sign-up before new worksheets
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a child's backpack leaning against an intake desk with blank forms

exampleSpecs.stakes: opening night lines will block fire exits
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she predicts signage is the answer, asks the focusing question, and instead opens one badge pickup lane that absorbs the whole queue
exampleSpecs.firstImage: laminated badges stacked beside a taped fire-exit line

exampleSpecs.stakes: healthy animals stay too long in kennels
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she uses the question to see that photo intake, not lobby posters, makes every later adoption easier
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a camera battery charging beside three empty kennel cards

exampleSpecs.stakes: round two cannot start until one table issue is fixed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he sees the one move was correcting a single mis-entered rating before printing every pairing sheet
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pairing sheet with one rating boxed in pencil

skillTargets: choose the next move instead of every move

tryThisNowSpec: Ask which one action would make the next visible obstacle easier, then write only the first physical step of that action.
